decisions.title: Screen orientation
decisions.question: Portrait (one thumb, like Clash Royale) or landscape (like MLBB)?
decisions.choice: Portrait
decisions.rationale: One-thumb play like Clash Royale; all three lanes visible at once.

impact.user: Played upright with one hand.
impact.technical: Field is tall and narrow; lanes are about a third of the screen width each.

approval.evidence: portrait

decisions.reviewTrigger: Players miss threats or hit the wrong lane in play tests.

decisions.title: Hero model
decisions.question: How do heroes work: a special card, a commander you move between lanes, or no hero?
decisions.choice: Hero cards that stay on the map; the player gives them orders (push, defend, gank, farm, retreat)
decisions.rationale: Adds Dota-style strategy (ganks, rotations, defence) without steering a hero by hand, which the research links to Star Wars: Force Arena failing.

impact.user: Drag a hero portrait onto the map to give an order; heroes fight on their own in between.
impact.technical: Hero AI with five orders, levels, respawn, hidden while in the jungle.

approval.evidence: special carrds, with players having the option to instruct the heroes to gank/defend basically strategising like in dota

decisions.reviewTrigger: Play tests show orders feel like a chore or are ignored.

decisions.title: Middle lane shape
decisions.question: Should the three lanes be the same?
options: Longer winding middle lane, symmetrical map
decisions.choice: The middle lane is longer (it winds) but the map stays symmetrical
decisions.rationale: Gives the middle lane its own identity: slower to push, decisive when its tower falls, close to both jungles.

impact.user: Middle pushes take longer; breaking the middle tower exposes the Core.
impact.technical: Lanes are waypoint paths; the map is the same when turned upside down.

approval.evidence: edit so that the mid lane is different, like make the middle lane longer but still simmetrical

decisions.reviewTrigger: The middle lane is always ignored or always the only lane that matters.

decisions.title: Hero abilities
decisions.question: Do hero abilities fire automatically or from a button the player taps?
decisions.choice: Automatically
decisions.rationale: Keeps the first test focused on orders and cards; less to track on a phone.

impact.user: No ability button to manage.
impact.technical: Hero AI decides when to use abilities.

approval.evidence: fire automatically

decisions.reviewTrigger: Players ask for more control over key moments.

decisions.title: Where the game lives
decisions.question: A new repository from the app-kit template, or a branch of the template?
decisions.choice: New repository (lane-game)
decisions.rationale: Keeps the template clean; the game has its own records and history.

impact.user: None.
impact.technical: Repository murshidihashim/lane-game; research and concept moved here.

approval.evidence: yes new repo

decisions.reviewTrigger: None.

decisions.title: World theme for heroes and names
decisions.question: Should heroes come from a rainforest world inspired by Southeast Asian folk tales, with Malay working names, or a generic fantasy world with English names?
options: Southeast Asian folk-tale world, Malay working names
decisions.choice: Proposed: Southeast Asian folk-tale inspired world with original characters and Malay working names
decisions.rationale: A look of its own next to medieval-fantasy card battlers, and it speaks to the first market (Malaysia, Indonesia, Philippines). Folklore inspires original characters; no religious figures, real people, spirits of the dead, or folk figures another game already uses.

impact.user: Hero, mana and Core names change (e.g. mana becomes Semangat).
impact.technical: Text and art only.

decisions.cost: none (names need roster and MyIPO checks before launch)

approval.evidence: go with the folk tale namez

decisions.reviewTrigger: Names fail a roster or trademark check, or playtesters outside the region find them hard to remember.

decisions.title: Hero power system v1
decisions.question: How do hero kits work?
options: Trait + Power + Ultimate at level 4 (once per life) + best-order bonus
One power only (as in the prototype)
decisions.choice: Proposed: Trait (always on) + Power (automatic, ranks at level 1-3) + Ultimate (level 4, once per life, automatic) + best-order bonus (+15% damage); pick 2 heroes before a match; no random effects
decisions.rationale: Dota-style growth during a match with Clash Royale-style readability; keeps powers automatic as decided in DEC-004, so the player plays heroes through orders.

impact.user: Heroes get stronger in steps; level 4 is a power spike; a pick-2-heroes screen before matches.
impact.technical: Ultimate flag per life, cooldown and ultimate rings on portraits, new effects (pull, stun, shield, reveal, transform).

approval.evidence: appriove power

decisions.reviewTrigger: Playtests show powers firing at bad moments too often.

decisions.title: Creep species and lane waves
decisions.question: How do creeps and troop cards work?
decisions.choice: Pick 1 of 5 species before the match. Each species has 3-4 troop classes. You choose which class marches in each lane's waves (change any time), and the same classes are your troop cards, plus one species spell and Petir.
decisions.rationale: Gives an RTS-style faction choice before the match and a lane-by-lane wave decision during it, while keeping Clash-style card play.

impact.user: A species pick before each match; a wave strip to choose each lane’s creep class.
impact.technical: Species and class data, per-lane waves, unit abilities, species spells.

approval.evidence: make the creep system be that there's 5 creep species / variants where players need to to choose at the start of the game, each creep species/variants will have 3-4 classes of troops which players can choose to deploy on each lane

decisions.reviewTrigger: Owner says per-lane waves or species cards are not what was meant.

decisions.title: Ward order and map rewards
decisions.question: What can heroes be told to do, and why go into the jungle?
decisions.choice: Orders: push tower, defend, gank, farm, ward, retreat. Map rewards: river fruit groves (Semangat), beast dens (hero buff), a river boss (Gajah Mina) that joins the killer's side, relics to collect, ward spots, and bounties for hero kills and towers.
decisions.rationale: Gives heroes reasons to leave the lanes (Dota-style map play) and makes vision a resource.

impact.user: Ward spots, groves, dens, a river boss, relics and bounties appear on the map; new order spots when dragging a hero.
impact.technical: Ward and relic entities, camp types, boss ally, bounties.

approval.evidence: give players the option to also instruct the heroes, say to gank, defend, push tower, farm, ward / create incentives on the map for heroes to explore, ward, farm, gank etc

decisions.reviewTrigger: Playtests show heroes ignore the map or matches swing too hard on the boss.

decisions.title: Art style
decisions.question: What should the game look like?
decisions.choice: Hikayat style: a hand-painted folk-tale board game seen from above. Batik and songket motifs, rainforest greens, red laterite paths, timber forts, chunky ink-outlined tokens with class glyphs, team colours indigo (you) and crimson (opponent).
decisions.rationale: Fits the folk-tale world (DEC-006), stays readable on a phone (tokens with glyphs, strong team colours), and can be drawn in code now and replaced by real art later.

impact.user: The whole game looks different but plays the same.
impact.technical: New drawing module; the map is drawn once and cached for speed.

approval.evidence: now simulate a cohesive artstyle as well

decisions.reviewTrigger: Owner prefers another direction, or the phone gets slow.

decisions.title: No hand-played cards: play through heroes and lane troops
decisions.question: How does the player act during a match?
decisions.choice: No cards in hand. Both picked heroes start on the map. During the match the player: gives hero orders (move anywhere, push, gank, defend, farm, ward, collect relic, retreat); buys items for heroes with Semangat; calls each hero's ultimate (the game suggests the best moment, the hero fires it at that moment); and chooses the troop class for each lane's waves. Species keep their troop classes; species spells and Petir are removed. Replaces the hero-as-card part of DEC-002, the automatic ultimate of DEC-004/DEC-007 and the deck part of DEC-008.
decisions.rationale: The owner wants strategy to come only from commanding heroes and choosing lane troops, closer to a MOBA commander game.

impact.user: No card row. Two hero panels with health, items and an ULT button; a Shop; wave chips stay.
impact.technical: Card, deck and spell systems removed; item stats, ult arming and a move order added; bot rewritten to match.

approval.evidence: remove troop cards being deployes by hand, players can only strategise by instructing heroes (move, buy items, ulti suggestion, gank) and selecting troops for each lanes ... introduce fog of war concept as well, clearly indicate health of the towers ... characters shouldnt be just dots, it needs to look like a character and ulti needs to visually show its effects on screen so players are aware on whats happening

decisions.reviewTrigger: Playtests show too little to do, or matches stall without cards.

decisions.title: Fog of war
decisions.question: What can each player see?
options: Vision from your own pieces; enemies outside it are hidden (built)
decisions.choice: Each side sees only around its own heroes, troops, towers, Pusaka and wards. Enemy heroes and troops outside that are not shown; the rest of the map is dimmed. Towers, the Pusaka and camps stay visible. The jungle still hides heroes inside vision unless a ward or a close enemy reveals them. The bot plays by the same vision for enemy heroes.
decisions.rationale: Makes wards, scouting and ganks matter; the owner asked for fog of war.

impact.user: Dark areas on the map; enemies appear when your pieces get close.
impact.technical: A shared, whole-number vision check in the rules; a fog layer in drawing.

approval.evidence: remove troop cards being deployes by hand, players can only strategise by instructing heroes (move, buy items, ulti suggestion, gank) and selecting troops for each lanes ... introduce fog of war concept as well, clearly indicate health of the towers ... characters shouldnt be just dots, it needs to look like a character and ulti needs to visually show its effects on screen so players are aware on whats happening

decisions.reviewTrigger: Players find the map too dark or lose track of the match.

decisions.title: Character figures, visible ultimates and tower health
decisions.question: How do heroes, troops, ultimates and tower health look?
options: Code-drawn character figures and ultimate effects (built)
decisions.choice: Heroes and troops are drawn as small characters (each hero with its own look, each troop class its own creature or fighter) on a team-coloured base, animated for walking and attacking, in the Hikayat style. Every ultimate shows a banner (who used what) and its own effect on the map. Towers show a large health bar with numbers, and the top bar shows every tower's health.
decisions.rationale: The owner asked for characters instead of dots and for ultimates players can see.

impact.user: Readable characters; clear ultimate moments; tower health at a glance.
impact.technical: Figure and effect drawing modules; ultimate events from the rules.

approval.evidence: remove troop cards being deployes by hand, players can only strategise by instructing heroes (move, buy items, ulti suggestion, gank) and selecting troops for each lanes ... introduce fog of war concept as well, clearly indicate health of the towers ... characters shouldnt be just dots, it needs to look like a character and ulti needs to visually show its effects on screen so players are aware on whats happening

decisions.reviewTrigger: Readability problems on a small phone, or a decision to commission real art.

decisions.title: Three heroes per player
decisions.question: How many heroes does each player command?
decisions.choice: Each player picks 3 heroes before the match. All three start at the Pusaka, one heading for each lane (in 2-lane mode the third joins the left lane). Each has its own panel with health, items and an ULT button. No hero can be on both sides.
decisions.rationale: The owner asked for 3 heroes each; with no hand cards, a third hero gives the player more to command.

impact.user: Three hero panels; three picks in the draft.
impact.technical: Hero count per player 3; HUD for 3 panels; bot and economy handle 3 heroes.

approval.evidence: do all the balance tunes first, each character should select 3 heroes, the loading screen where you select heroes should be like dota/tekken

decisions.reviewTrigger: Playtests show 3 heroes are too many to manage on a phone.

decisions.title: Draft-style hero select and versus screen
decisions.question: How does the hero selection screen look and work?
options: Draft screen with turns, big hero preview, roster grid and a versus screen (built)
decisions.choice: After choosing a species, a draft: you and the bot take turns picking (you 1, bot 1, you 2, bot 1... a snake order), shown as two rows of 3 slots facing each other. The highlighted hero stands large on a lit stage with its name, role and powers; a roster grid of 20 portraits below; picked heroes are taken. Then a versus screen shows both line-ups and species, with a short loading bar, before the match. Original Hikayat look (night, songket gold), no borrowed art.
decisions.rationale: The owner wants the selection to feel like a fighting-game or MOBA draft: a moment of build-up and counter-picking.

impact.user: A dramatic pick screen and a versus screen before each match.
impact.technical: New draft screen module; deterministic bot draft picks so matches still replay.

approval.evidence: do all the balance tunes first, each character should select 3 heroes, the loading screen where you select heroes should be like dota/tekken

decisions.reviewTrigger: The draft feels slow on repeat matches (a quick rematch skips it).

decisions.title: Slower movement and a zoomable map
decisions.question: How do we make the map feel bigger and the pieces less rushed?
options: Slower movement plus a zoomable, pannable map view (built)
decisions.choice: All troops and heroes move about 30% slower (attacks and powers unchanged), and walking animations follow the distance actually walked. The map keeps showing the whole battlefield by default; you can zoom in (zoom button, double-tap, or pinch) up to 2x and drag to look around, and zoom back out the same way.
decisions.rationale: The owner felt the map was small or the pieces too fast. Slower movement gives fights, ganks and rotations more room; a zoom makes the characters and map bigger on a phone without losing the whole-map view.

impact.user: Calmer pace; a zoom button on the map; drag to pan when zoomed.
impact.technical: Speed numbers in the rules; camera (zoom and pan) in the screen layer; map painted at higher resolution.

approval.evidence: the map feels slightly small/or the characters are just moving too fast ... think of balance changes ... polish the character designs and animations please

decisions.reviewTrigger: Matches feel slow or zooming gets in the way of giving orders.

decisions.title: Hero command menu, Attack order and smarter heroes
decisions.question: How does a player command a hero, and how much do heroes think for themselves?
options: Tap hero, pick an order from a menu, tap the target (built; dragging a portrait stays as a shortcut)
Drag the portrait onto a spot only (as before)
decisions.choice: Tap a hero (its panel or the hero on the map) to open its command menu: Move, Attack, Push, Gank, Defend, Farm, Ward, Retreat. Pick one and the map highlights only the valid targets with a hint ("Tap a lane"), and Cancel; tap a target to give the order (Retreat is instant). New Attack order: pick a visible enemy hero, troop, tower or ward and the hero goes after it, then returns to its job. Heroes are smarter on their own: they pass through their own troops, slide past each other, wait outside an enemy tower until their own troops are there to take the hits, fall back towards their own tower when badly hurt while pushing, and pick targets better (enemy heroes in reach first, then the weakest).
decisions.rationale: The owner found drag-to-order unintuitive and saw heroes stall after orders; a menu with highlighted targets is the familiar pattern, and the AI changes stop heroes stalling or throwing their lives away.

impact.user: Tap a hero, choose, tap a target; heroes keep moving and look after themselves; a new Attack order.
impact.technical: Collision fix; hero AI rules (tower dive, fall back, target choice); Attack order in the rules; command menu in the screen layer.

approval.evidence: make it so that heroes are smarter, now currently the heroes would suddenly stop moving after commands are given ... make the instruction for heroes more intuitive, it should be player clicking on the hero's icon, select a few available option, and target where to go/what to aim etc etc

decisions.reviewTrigger: Players feel heroes act on their own too much, or the menu is slow.

decisions.title: Art direction for the full game
decisions.question: Which look should the full game grow into, once real art is made?
options: 1. Hikayat board game, painted by an artist (the current look, finished by hand)
3. Wayang kulit 'living puppets' (coloured, jointed leather puppets on a lamp-lit board)
4. Batik paper-cut diorama, 2.5D (layered paper and batik, die-cut standees)
5. Anime cel-shaded 2D (line art, two-tone shading, splash portraits)

6. Anime heroes with Malay heritage art: cel-shaded anime figures with thick outlines, one signature Malay pattern per hero, and ultimates drawn as heritage art (batik, songket, wayang). Added after the owner's reference: Demon Slayer
decisions.choice: Option 4: batik paper-cut diorama. The board is layers of cut paper and batik-printed cloth with soft shadows; characters are die-cut paper standees with a white cut edge; forts are folded paper; the menus are paper cards on indigo batik cloth. It replaces the Hikayat look.
decisions.rationale: The owner chose it. It is distinctive and Malaysian (batik; local precedents Kabaret and Paper Ghost Stories: 7PM), close to the existing flat standee engine, and the white cut edge keeps figures apart from the board. Readability rule: busy batik texture stays on the board and menus, low in contrast; figures stay plain. Evidence: REP-010, REP-011, docs/research/art-style-options.md.

impact.user: The whole game looks different (map, characters, forts, fog, menus, draft); play is unchanged.
impact.technical: Drawing code only (src/ui, index.html). Map and figures stay cached; paper shadows and cut edges are drawn once per cache entry. No new dependency.

decisions.cost: RM0 (code-drawn). Real art by an artist later would be a separate, paid decision.

approval.evidence: use the batik paper card diorama

decisions.reviewTrigger: The paper look reads poorly on the owner's phone, phones slow down, or the owner changes direction.

decisions.title: Map view fills the screen width
decisions.question: Should the map be shown whole (narrow, with empty sides) or fill the screen's width and scroll?
options: Keep the whole map in view (narrow on phones whose browser bars take height)
Fill the screen width and scroll up and down, with a whole-map view on the corner button (chosen)
Reshape the map to be wider and shorter (changes the game rules and balance)
decisions.choice: The map fills the screen's width (the usual view), starting at your side; drag up and down to look around. The corner button shows the whole map and comes back; double-tap or pinch zooms closer. Tapping a hero's panel scrolls to that hero if it is off-screen. Updates DEC-016's zoom: zoom 1 is now the whole-map overview, not the starting view.
decisions.rationale: The owner asked for it. On a phone browser the whole map was often only about 260 px wide on a 390 px screen. The world, lanes and balance are unchanged; only the camera changes.

impact.user: A bigger map that fills the screen; drag to see the far side; corner button for the whole map.
impact.technical: Camera and layout only (src/ui/layout.ts, game.ts, render.ts, art.ts map painter). No change to src/game.

approval.evidence: lets expand the map now so it fits the width of the screen

decisions.reviewTrigger: Players lose track of the far side of the map (then add a mini-map), or the owner prefers the whole-map view.

decisions.title: Make the map more engaging
decisions.question: Which of five map ideas should be built next?
options: 1. Monsoon, dry season and night: the map changes every 90 s or so (flooded river, walkable shallows, shorter sight at night), each announced 10 s ahead
2. Kampung outposts: two or three jungle villages a hero captures by standing in them; they give vision, a little Semangat and a place to heal, and can be retaken
3. Pasar malam merchant: a travelling night-market stall appears in the jungle now and then, selling one rare item to the first hero who reaches it
4. Lalang grass and startled birds: tall-grass patches beside the lanes hide whoever stands in them; birds burst out of the grass and trees when hidden heroes pass, a readable tell through the fog
5. A living paper map: fireflies, river ripples, kitchen smoke, towers that collapse into paper scraps and battle marks that stay (no rules change)
decisions.choice: Not chosen yet. Suggested start: 5 (cheap, no rules change) plus 1 (the biggest change to how matches feel).
decisions.rationale: Each idea adds a decision or a moment rather than more buttons, in line with the research finding that hybrids failed by adding load. Details, effort and risks: REP-013.

impact.user: More reasons to move around the map and more changing moments in a match.
impact.technical: Options 1-4 change the game rules (deterministic, need new tests and a balance run); 5 is drawing only.

decisions.reviewTrigger: The owner picks one or more, or playtests show the map already has enough going on.

decisions.title: Hero controls that keep the map clear
decisions.question: Which way of commanding heroes should replace the pop-up order menu, which covers part of the map?
options: 1. Order cards: tap a hero, and a row of order cards (Move, Attack, Push, Gank, Defend, Farm, Ward, Retreat) replaces the lane chips under the map; drag a card onto its target on the map

2. Smart drag: drag a hero's portrait onto the map; the order follows what you drop it on (own tower = Defend, a lane = Push, an enemy = Attack, a camp = Farm, a cairn = Ward, home = Retreat, open ground = Move), with a label at your finger before you let go
3. Ring menu: press and hold a hero; six small order icons fan out round your thumb; slide to one and let go on the target

4. Tactic cards: build a deck of 8 team tactics before the match (e.g. All push left, Gank mid together, Hold the line, Jungle sweep); hold 3 in the match and play one with Semangat to order all three heroes at once, with a short bonus
5. Lane board: a one-row strip under the map with Left, Mid, Right, Jungle and Home slots; drag hero tokens between slots to reassign them (top of a slot = push, bottom = defend)
decisions.choice: Option 3: the ring menu. Press a hero (its panel, or the hero on the map) and its eight orders fan out in a ring round your thumb; slide onto one and let go, then tap the target, or keep sliding out of the ring onto the target and let go there. A quick tap opens the ring so you can tap an order. While aiming, the hint and Cancel sit in the lane-chip row, so nothing covers the map. Replaces the DEC-017 order menu and the portrait-drag shortcut.
decisions.rationale: The owner chose it. It covers only a thumb's width round the finger, appears where the player is already looking, and one press-slide-release gives a complete order.

impact.user: A new way to give every order; the old pop-up menu and the drag shortcut are gone.
impact.technical: Screen and input code only (src/ui/game.ts, render.ts, layout.ts, placement.ts) and the phone check. No change to src/game.

approval.evidence: go with idea 3

decisions.reviewTrigger: Players find the ring hard to discover or miss-select orders on small phones.

decisions.title: Character design target: Dota 2 quality bar
decisions.question: Should heroes and troops keep the cute big-headed board-piece look, or move to heroic, detailed designs?
options: Heroic, detailed designs at the Dota 2 quality bar, still our own folk-tale characters in the batik paper style (chosen)
decisions.choice: Heroic designs at the Dota 2 quality bar: about five heads tall, broad shoulders, layered costumes (pauldrons, chest armour, belts, skirts, bracers, boots, capes), one big signature shape per hero, the value pattern Valve describes (dark feet, light head and shoulders), glow accents on magic users, and simpler, species-themed troops in team colours. Dota 2 is the quality target only: no hero, name, costume or shape is copied; every character stays an original Malay folk-tale design, cut from paper (DEC-018).
decisions.rationale: The owner asked for Dota 2 as the target. Valve's published character art guide stresses a silhouette readable at a glance and a value gradient from dark lower body to light head and upper body. Copying Dota 2 designs is ruled out by the project's originality rule.

impact.user: Every hero and troop looks new; play is unchanged.
impact.technical: Drawing code only (src/ui/figures.ts, render sizes, portraits, draft stage). No change to src/game.

approval.evidence: okay now lets do a thorough enhancement of heroes and creep design, take Dota 2 characters as the target of what we want to be

decisions.reviewTrigger: Figures read worse at play size, phones slow down, or the owner wants a different direction.
